critical.issue: ROUTE ORDERING BUG. In /app/backend/server.py the dynamic /staff/{staff_id}/ical-info (line 3310) is registered BEFORE the static /staff/team/ical-info (line 3325), and same for /staff/{staff_id}/ical (line 3282) vs /staff/team/ical (line 3297). FastAPI matches in registration order, so `staff_id='team'` shadows the team endpoints. Confirmed: /api/staff/team/ical-info returns 404 'User not found' (from _ensure_ical_token → user lookup for id='team') instead of 200 with the team token. /api/staff/team/ical also gets routed to the individual handler and will only ever return 403 'Invalid token' — the team token check code path is unreachable in production. FIX: move the two /staff/team/... route decorators ABOVE the /staff/{staff_id}/... ones (e.g. put lines 3297 & 3325 before 3282 & 3310).

rca of the issue: The team-iCal 404 is a classic FastAPI/Starlette route-ordering pitfall: when both `@api.get('/staff/{staff_id}/ical-info')` and `@api.get('/staff/team/ical-info')` are registered, whichever is declared FIRST in the source file wins the match. In /app/backend/server.py the dynamic path is declared at line 3310 (individual) and 3282 (individual /ical), and the static team path at line 3325 and 3297 respectively — so ANY GET /api/staff/team/ical-info request is captured by the dynamic handler with `staff_id='team'`, and `_ensure_ical_token('team')` raises 404 because no user has id='team'. Reproduction: `curl <BASE>/api/staff/team/ical-info -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin>' → 404`. Mitigation: two-line move — reorder the decorators so the static team routes are registered BEFORE the dynamic staff_id routes, or (better) add an explicit path parameter constraint like `@api.get('/staff/{staff_id:uuid}/ical-info')` if staff_id is always a UUID.
